title: Van Dedem (Constantinople) to Van de Spiegel and the Agent van Staat, 1788-1799 (DECODE R2120, R2122, R2131, R1895)

steps.what: Fetched metadata and images for the 4 records and 10 sibling records named in the DECODE notes.
Sibling records R2121, R1947 and R2053 are marked decrypted; R2121 holds the same cipher pages as R2120 plus their full clear decipherment.
Searched DECODE key records; checked the undated Fagel key series R2842-R2852, which are large alphabetical Dutch codebooks and not this code.
Transcribed R2122 and R2131, and the R2121, R1947 and R2053 cipher pages and their solutions (two agents).
Found heavy homophony (de x36 in the clear text, no group used more than 11 times) and that only 52-58% of the target groups occur in any crib.
Tested an alphabetical code order against anchored words.
Hard-EM, then leave-one-out word aligners with restarts, over the cipher and decipherment pairs.
Treated the hundreds digit as a dummy (thousands digit + last two digits) and re-aligned.

Second pass (Feyseel Nur, PR #21): groups re-indexed as T*1000 + (H>=5)*500 + line*5 + (H mod 5); the crib values from R2121, R1947 and R2053 then follow alphabetical order within each 500-group block (Spearman 0.799 for five columns, against 0.351 numeric order and a permutation null p99.9 of 0.368; OpenAI Codex re-derivation in alpha/codex_review/).

R2122 and R2131 decoded with the 354-value table graded A/B/C plus alphabetical brackets for unknown groups (alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt): firm values on 123 of 301 non-null groups; the loan theme of R2122 agrees with R2121.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R1895 (1799) is in a marked system of 2-3-digit groups with superscript marks, not the 1788-93 homophonic word code of R2120/R2122/R2131, so it is its own entry (dedem1799); the 1788-93 letters stay in dedem1788.

Catalogue audit: profile, page and README brought into line with the second pass (they still said 'not solved' and 'not alphabetical'); fraction of firm values measured from alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 130 tokens, 80 types, nl-modern order 4: reading -2.009 per letter; random keys -2.142 (z 2.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.651 (mean -1.684, z -10.0); annealer on the real text -1.702. Verdict: underdetermined.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked tx/ transcriptions (R2121 cipher = the two R2120 pages), the contemporary clear decipherment tx/R2121_clear.txt, and the graded partial decoding of R2122/R2131 in alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt; key = alpha/dedem_alpha_table.tsv.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). alpha/decoded_targets_v2.txt read group by group: R2122 (A+B 40%) and R2131 (16 of 46 firm) have holes in nearly every clause; only the clear passages read (docs/_check_reading.py: 4 of 113 sentences clean). Both relabelled decoded, not read. R2120 reads from its contemporary decipherment tx/R2121_clear.txt (continuous Dutch; reading_review A). Method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> read from existing decipherment (parts); fraction_read 0.41 -> 0.673 (R2120 groups of all three letters).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b19): DECODE R2122 and R2131 re-fetched with the project cookie (b19_fetch.py): images only (2 and 4), no attachment, transcription or comment; every image opened, no contemporary decipherment. Sibling records with solutions (R1948-R1952, R2132-R2134, R2141) fetched and listed.

The legation inventory (NA 1.02.20, targets/roell1809/turk_inv.txt) lists under Kroll (1784-85) inv. 785 'Sleutel geheimschrift'. Its 6 scans on the Nationaal Archief site (b19_na_fetch.py) are a bound codebook headed 'Kroll. Un Chiffre': 500-group pages of five columns of 100, words alphabetical across the rows, letters and syllables in a table at the foot of each column, names and titles in 3001-3500, a Nota on noun and preterite forms. It is this code: the slot model's A-grade values recur (2 aan, 17 als, 86 de, 238 belang, 541 en, 1124 het, 1764 oorlog, 3273 Porta). inv. 686 (De Weiler, 1775) holds the Berigt on begin/einde des briefs markers and nulls.

All 238 distinct groups of R2122 and R2131 looked up on the codebook scans (b19_keylook.py; key/kroll785_values.tsv); 237 found, 4414 does not exist. The cipher re-read on the DECODE images: R2131 2261 -> 2262 (sig), 311 -> 317? (als dat); R2122 clear salutation and close added (tx/*_corrections.tsv). The slot model's values differ from the book at 16, 194, 526, 675, 1455 (instructie, not interest), 1069, 3610 (de Envoyé van Pruissen).

R2122 and R2131 decoded with the codebook (b19_dedem_decode.py) and read sentence by sentence, joining words the code spells in pieces (el+der+s, du+r+ven, ver+ne+der+ing); every unbracketed word checked as carried (b19_wordcheck.py). Readings tx/R2122_reading.md and tx/R2131_reading.md with English. Clean-sentence share: checker's modern Dutch list 0.222 and 0.200; explicit holes only 0.933 and 0.800. Open: 1230, 1330, 80, 760 (twice, after an infinitive: probably the Nota's example number copied for a 'g' character, not adopted), 4414, 3928, 1605, 1463, 319, 591.

Consistency pass (cl): the read bar failed on the gap 'R2120: English translation not yet written' (not-attempted), but tx/R2121_en.md was written on 23 Oct 2026 (translation wave, 130be0109) and is already outcome.texts[0].translation: a stale gap, removed from outcome.gaps and NOTES.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 3 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Nationaal Archief EAD search located S.E. Croiset's cipher-office papers, NA 2.21.045 (familie Croiset) A.7.b, 1789-1810: inv. 18 correspondence with Dutch envoys on setting cipher codes, with cipher letters and code tables; inv. 21 cipher codes with notes and instructions to envoys; inv. 22 letter from W.F. Roell. All PHYSICAL, not scanned.

Issue #244 (EscalatorStudios): code 2704 was entered as 'anno 2 voorige jaar'. Scan 0004 of NA 1.02.20 inv. 785 (downloaded from the reporter's link) read directly: the faded entry in the 'te meer' cell, row 4, is the abbreviation 'ann.t 2 voorige Car.s', annuleert 2 voorige caracters (cancel the 2 preceding characters). Key table corrected, R2122 decode regenerated with b19_dedem_decode.py (one line changes); no reading changes (the opener 2504 2604 2704 was never read). The reporter's comparison entry 1429 on scan 0002 not settled.

texts.label: R2120 (cipher pages re-photographed as R2121), Pera 22 Dec 1788
texts.summary: Van Dedem, Dutch ambassador at Constantinople, reports to Grand Pensionary Van de Spiegel the Porte's proposed loan of 7-8 million, secured on the revenues of Morea, Negropont, Salonica, Volos, Urfan, Cara Agatz, Damascus, Sorien and Rodosto and the tribute of Jenischeher, and suggests the Levant Directors or Hope & Co. take it up. The decryption is the contemporary clear decipherment filed as R2121.

reading_review.note: The contemporary clear decipherment (tx/R2121_clear.txt) reads as continuous Dutch: the Porte's proposed loan of 7-8 million and its securities. It is the decipherment of this cipher, not a separate clear letter, so R2120 reads from an existing decipherment; the low score is the word list's coverage of 18th-century Dutch spelling.

texts.label: R2122, "Duplicaat", Pera 15 Jan 1789
texts.summary: Two cipher blocks (258 groups) in a clear letter to Van de Spiegel, decoded in part with the block-alphabetical table of the second pass; the firm words (envoyé, Porta, negociatie, Republicq, Leening) are consistent with the loan theme of the R2121 crib. Values, not sense: the running reading is fragmentary.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b19) with the codebook itself, 'Kroll. Un Chiffre', Nationaal Archief 1.02.20 (legatie Turkije) inv. 785: every group looked up on the scans (key/kroll785_values.tsv), the cipher re-read on the DECODE images, clear salutation and close transcribed; the whole letter reads (Van Dedem's demarches after the resolution of 2 October, the Porte's wish for a loan negotiation in the Republic passed to the Prussian envoy, his distrust of the English ambassador, a Swedish subsidy). Holes: 1230, 1330 (twice), 80, 760 (twice), 4414 (no such code), 3928, 1605, 1463 give no sense where they stand. Clean-sentence share of the body 0.222 on the checker's modern Dutch list, 0.933 counting explicit holes only (period spelling, as for battier1686).

texts.label: R2131, Pera 9 Feb 1793
texts.summary: One cipher paragraph of 50 groups in a clear letter to Van de Spiegel, decoded in part (16 of 46 non-null groups firm); it names the Porte, an envoy, the war and the French, but the neutrality reading proposed in review is not established.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b19) with the codebook 'Kroll. Un Chiffre' (NA 1.02.20 inv. 785): the Ottoman Porte bound itself to the Prussian envoy the day before yesterday to stay neutral in the war with the French and make no further alliance with that nation. Transcription corrected on the DECODE image (2261 -> 2262, 311 -> 317?); open: 319 (Son Altesse where 'alle' is needed), 591 ('g' after 'verbond'). Clean-sentence share 0.200 on the checker's modern Dutch list, 0.800 counting explicit holes only.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 87.2% of the words of tx/R2131_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
